verdict.rationale: Obsidian has no dedicated way to version, review or roll back automations, but its automation artifacts (templates, plugin code, Bases) live as plain-text files in the vault. That means note-level tools can cover them indirectly: Obsidian Sync's version history lets you view or restore previous versions of a note, and Git-based sync or the community Git plugin can track file changes. This is an indirect workaround, not first-class automation lifecycle management. Missing for 10: automation-specific versioning, diff/review of automation changes before they run, explicit rollback of plugin or automation configuration, and any independent evidence that Sync history or Git is actually used to manage automations.
